title: Startup taps underwater volcano as energy source in "proof point" test
gist: Seattle startup Endurance Energy ran the first subsea geothermal power demo at the Axial Seamount, about 5,000 ft deep: its 100 kW Adélie plant ran net-positive for only about 8.7 seconds (median about 2 kW, peak 16.5 kW) on a natural vent after its drilled 2-inch well delivered too little fluid, before a software fault and a cable short ended the trial. The company plans a 2 MW commercial deployment of up to six generators for diesel-dependent Tonga in 2027, while a Stanford expert warns that the extra cost of going subsea could make geothermal uncompetitive.

themes.theme: Subsea geothermal proof point: thin results

insights.claim: Endurance Energy's 100 kW Adélie subsea geothermal plant was net-positive for only about 8.7 seconds, producing a median of about 2 kW and a peak of 16.5 kW of net power, and 60 watt-hours over nearly half a minute at about 26,000 rpm.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: This proves feasibility but delivers only a tiny fraction of nameplate output, so commercial claims are still unproven.

insights.claim: CEO Andrew Redd calls net-positive output the threshold that matters, claiming no one had previously generated more power than it took to run a plant on the seafloor.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Expect fundraising narratives built on 'world first' claims, so weigh them against how long the plant actually ran.
insights.quote: “Net-positive is the threshold that matters: the plant made more power than it took to run itself on the seafloor, which no one had done before.”

insights.claim: The net-positive run happened on a natural hydrothermal vent (about 538°F) only because the drilled well could not supply enough fluid, and Redd says future deployments will rely on drilled wells.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The headline result does not validate the commercial model, which depends on wells, since that part has not yet produced power.
insights.locator: Placing the geothermal plant on top

insights.claim: A battery module current spike that made the control software halt on stale readings, and a power cable that shorted when seawater seeped through a casing flaw, ended Endurance Energy's trial.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Basic reliability of subsea electrical and software systems remains the core execution risk.

insights.claim: Endurance Energy drilled two holes about 5,000 ft (1,524 m) deep that vented fluid at about 500°F, but the cased test well was only 52 ft deep and 2 inches wide, versus the 20-36 inch casings typical of oil, gas, and onshore geothermal wells.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Scaling well size and depth is unproven, and that is where capex and technical risk will concentrate.
insights.locator: The test well was also just 2 inches

insights.claim: Endurance's current lander drill can reach about 260 ft (80 m), five times deeper than the test well, and the company expects deeper wells to deliver enough fluid.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The next milestone to watch is whether deeper drilled wells sustain flow.
insights.quote: “That limited how much fluid it could deliver, and deeper wells should change that.”

insights.claim: The deployment relied on shared third-party infrastructure: Stabbert Maritime's ship Ocean Guardian, Canada's ROPOS submersible, and the NSF-funded, University of Washington-operated 559-mile Regional Cabled Array for power and connectivity.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Commercial sites will lack this subsidized research infrastructure, so expect costs to rise.
insights.locator: Adélie also connected to Endurance Energy’s

insights.claim: Stanford's Roland Horne says subsea geothermal is probably technically feasible but would undoubtedly cost more than land geothermal, which is already only on the edge of being price-competitive.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Subsea geothermal is unlikely to compete in markets with cheap alternatives and will need niche markets with high fuel costs.
insights.quote: “It’s probably technically feasible, but it would undoubtedly be more expensive than to do it on land,”

insights.claim: Redd argues the deep ocean provides unlimited cold seawater for cooling and pressure that keeps the system and well pressurized, allowing compact plants.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: These physical advantages are the company's whole cost argument, so look for data that proves them.
insights.quote: “The deep ocean gives us unlimited cold seawater for cooling, and its weight keeps the system and the well pressurized, so our plants can be compact,”

insights.claim: Endurance Energy plans its first commercial deployment with the Kingdom of Tonga in 2027, using up to six shipping-container-sized 2 MW generators offshore.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Up to about 12 MW is the first real revenue test, but schedule risk is high given the trial results.
insights.locator: The company is also developing a larger 2-megawatt

insights.claim: Tonga's grid runs mainly on imported diesel, whose price has risen significantly since the US and Israel launched their war with Iran, strengthening the case for local renewables in island nations.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: High oil prices from the war widen the cost gap that makes premium-priced subsea renewables viable for islands that import fuel.
insights.locator: The Polynesian island nation in the South Pacific

insights.claim: Redd names the US Pacific Northwest and Alaska, Taiwan, and Japan as large markets with ample offshore geothermal resources, and expects to eventually compete on cost with continuous, weather-independent power.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: The addressable market is large but depends on reliable operation in Tonga first.

insights.claim: Endurance Energy's next trial, in winter 2026-2027, will use a refurbished, upgraded Adélie renamed Gentoo that aims to sustain higher power generation.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Gentoo is the next checkpoint for whether the plant can run sustained.
